forecaster_note: Mon: easing ENE/NE swell, head high to slightly overhead early, brief offshore around dawn then a southerly change — sheltered southern corners hold clean. Tue: S swell head-high to overhead at southern magnets, chest high on E-facing beaches, light offshore early then onshore. — Surfline forecaster, Mon 26 Oct

days.label: Today
days.note: Easing NE/ENE swell (762 kJ, 10s) but southerly already in at 6am — dawn offshore gone. Go S end of Curl Curl / Manly corner; exposures bumpy. Light showers.
days.surfline_text: Nice mix of easing ENE / NE swell for the early with head to maybe slightly overhead surf at most spots. Perhaps a brief offshore window around dawn otherwise S winds. Sheltered southern corners probably the best bet for lasting clean surf. Once the south change is through we'll see slowly building surf at exposures into the overhead range but junky and onshore - sheltered southern corners continue clean to cleanish all day with fun sized surf from easing ENE swell mix.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: S swell arrives (head-high at southern magnets, chest on E-facing; Dee Why wraps poorly off S). Light offshore until ~noon — best AM window of the week.
days.surfline_text: S swell delivers head high to overhead surf at the southern magnets, chest high or so surf on the E facing beaks, smaller for shelter. Light, variable offshore winds offer a promising early morning window, with clean conditions at most breaks Then from later morning S swell gradually eases, with chest to head high sets at the S exposures. Moderate onshore winds develop, adding bump and reducing quality.
